label: sequence contains 3/d/t/x; peaks when about to output 3
explanation: Dense feature (43% of steps, nearly every sequence), mostly weak. The strong activations are tied to token identity in the original sequence, especially the digit 3, then d, t, x (r, b, g, y less so). Activation is highest at the step whose output is 3 (out_tok==3: 97% active, 12% of mass, top-quartile steps), and high one step earlier (next_out==3) and at <DEL> in sequences whose first token is 3. In the original phase it rises gradually after a 3 or d has been input. When the output is one of these tokens it fires with high precision (out_tok in {3,d,t,x}: precision 0.90), but that covers only 28% of mass. The recorded predicate (sequence contains 3/d/t/x, and we are past <DEL>, or one has already been seen, or t<2) captures about 83% of mass at roughly 0.54 precision. Weak, low-level activation on sequences with none of these tokens is not explained. It does not depend on L, copy correctness, or repeated tokens.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by phase (copy phase: 3, d, t, x; input phase: 1, n, a, k; delimiter step: <DEL>) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: 3, d, t, x; delimiter step: 3, d, t, r; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: t=1, L=9 & t=8, L=3 & t=3.
